editorial:
Imagine starting a new job and wanting everything to be perfect, only to have it blow up in your face. That is exactly what happens to Dārta, a teacher who just wants a professional meeting with the parents of her 9th grade class. Instead of a serious discussion about graduation, you get a room full of adults acting like toddlers. You have Žanete trying too hard to be the favorite with gifts, a couple in an open marriage playing games, and exes who cannot stop fighting. It is a chaotic mess that feels like a pressure cooker, and you will find yourself laughing at how quickly everything falls apart.

The acting is the best part here because the actors make these annoying characters feel like real people you might actually know. The pacing is quick, and the arguments build up in a way that feels natural and funny. While some of the fights get a bit loud, the payoff is worth it.
endingExplained: After the meeting turns into a giant shouting match, the parents finally stop fighting when they realize how embarrassing they look in front of Dārta. The twist is that the students actually burst into the room and reveal they have been filming the whole disaster for a school project. Everyone feels silly, and they finally agree on a graduation plan. Dārta realizes she cannot control the parents, but she earns their respect for surviving the madness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward situations and family comedies.
